question: Can an explicit discrete surface inverse and independently refined calibration resolve the unfitted fourth-order response on two incident spectra?

method.action: Unchanged SS OCF 1 radial Hamiltonian; exact formal neutral A,A3 and core/clock A0,A2,A4 coefficients, including quadrature logarithm square term.
method.domain: Regular origin, R=80 and domain control R=100; h=.1,.05,.025,.0125. Independent BVP/Newton core and independent clock eigenmode at fixed omega_Q=.9. Readout omega_chi=.41274991 stays fixed.
method.boundaries: Zero radial fields at outer boundary, T=60 before any outer reflection returns. Local r=.1; surface r=14.
method.initial_data: b compact in known [18,26], v=D_h b. Two shapes unknown to inverse: cos^4 envelope center22 width3.25 and width2.5 times cos(1.4(r-22)). A=.008,+/-.012, quiet receiver. Clock amplitude .001 and phase0.
method.solver: RK4 plus exact adjoint of the discrete acquisition propagator. Surface b and b_t every .025 through t16. SVD inverse cutoff1e-10 and1e-8 control. Predictors receive support/incoming rule but not shape. Output .025 with decimated .05 control. Nonlinear receivers follow all locked forecasts.
method.tolerances: Nominal A=.012. B=|Yfinest-Yfiner|+|Yfinest-Ytime|+|Ywide-Yfiner|+|P4inverse-P4finest|+max sampling interval change+2e-11 cycles. Require B<=|P4-P2|/4. See protocol for marker, convergence and decision rules.

hypotheses.prediction: Discrete inversion removes coarse propagation mismatch; a converged fourth-order correction improves both spectra by more than the complete numerical budget.
A persistent resolved phase/timing residual rejects the extension; insufficient numerical resolution leaves it unresolved.

controls.method: Independently resolve the same omega_Q branch and mode without fitting omega_chi; prior interpolated fine profile is a labeled diagnostic.

controls.purpose: Bound mesh, time, box, sampling, and inverse error
controls.method: Four meshes, finest half-dt, wide box, Hermite decimation, fixed alternate SVD cutoff.
Broad shell and carrier-modulated shell; signed amplitudes; no nonlinear receiver before all forecast locks.
